idea-plugin.name: Local Push Mock
idea-plugin.description:
Test Android push notifications from Android Studio — no backend, no Firebase credentials.

Local Push Mock lets you fire a real Android notification on any device or emulator straight from the IDE. Fill in a form, click Send notification, and it shows up as if your production push had just arrived.

Before you start, read the User Guide on GitLab: the plugin needs a small debug-only library added to your app.

Use it to

  • Check how your notifications look: title, body, channel, importance and icon.
  • Test deep links and the data payload your app receives when the notification is tapped.
  • Reproduce push scenarios without waiting for the backend or touching the Firebase console.
  • Run your own production notification code through an optional hook.

How it works

The plugin sends the notification to your app over adb. A tiny receiver that exists only in your debug build shows it using the native Android APIs, mimicking a real FCM push. Nothing ships to production, and other apps cannot trigger it.

Requirements

  • Android Studio Ladybug (2024.2) or later
  • An Android device or emulator (Android 5.0+)
  • The localpush-debug library in your app's debug build — setup steps on GitLab
